cards.front: Pelvic pain on most days for [___] or more is persistent (chronic) pelvic pain.
cards.context: Persistent pelvic pain is pain on most days in the pelvis. Some definitions use 3 months; Australian guidance commonly uses 6.

cards.front: A 52-year-old with disabling hot flushes is anticoagulated for a deep vein thrombosis diagnosed four weeks ago. The vasomotor treatment that is contraindicated now is [___].
cards.context:
Active or recent venous thromboembolism contraindicates menopausal hormone therapy.

Non-hormonal options, such as an SSRI, SNRI or gabapentin, can treat vasomotor symptoms instead.
